status: First model-layer separation and seam groove/ridge comparison reported by Derek
authority: Direct user report and two supplied photographs
operator_observation_quote: I am letting the print continue so we get scarf results, but I can see already that all 3 faucet bases have the lifting problem.

operator_model_layer_observation.quote: In these faucet base prints, at that "lifting" area, the first layer just falls off, it is not connected to the layers above it all. So this lifting is actually "perfect removal" for the removal I was initially seeking, before I realized that was removing the first layer.
operator_model_layer_observation.layer_identity: The first model layer above the supports
operator_model_layer_observation.location: The affected lower front lip of the faucet base specimens
operator_model_layer_observation.physical_result: The first model layer falls away and is reported to have no connection to the model layers above.
operator_model_layer_observation.removal_interpretation: The easy removal sheds model material. Clean release alone does not establish an intact supported underside.
operator_model_layer_observation.evidence_scope: Derek's direct observation of these faucet base prints; no per-specimen bond-strength measurement or initiating sequence supplied.

photo_observations.observation: A dark opening is visible along the lower front curved lip immediately above the support interface on all three foot specimens. The native plate maps the front row left-to-right to A, B and C.
The close-up shows a dark horizontal slit under the front curved wall. The opening is widest through the middle, while the ends are much closer to the support interface.
photo_observations.identification_limit: The supplied close-up is not labeled with an individual specimen letter.

scarf_results.operator_quote:
Fascinating. "E" and "F" are identical as far as I can tell.

But, "D" is clearly a groove while "E/F" is clearly a ridge. And this is true for both the 0.08 layers and 0.24 layers.
scarf_results.scope: Derek's direct appearance comparison; no measured groove/ridge dimensions or strength result

inference: The founder reports replication on A, B and C under the three model-cooling treatments and identifies the affected material as the first model layer separating from the layers above. No cooling winner or severity ranking is recorded.
measurement_limits: A support clearance is programmed. Derek establishes first model-layer separation in the affected region. The photographs do not quantify excess separation; initiating movement, physical strand position during deposition, cause of the missing connection and any nozzle contact remain unresolved.
disposition: Plate completed and bed cleared by Derek; coarse-start and seam-gap comparisons authorized on one subsequent plate
scope: First model-layer separation on A/B/C and the regular seam groove versus scarf ridge Derek reported on D/E/F at both layer heights; no quantitative bond-strength, seam profile or causal result

coarse_recovery_hypothesis.quote: 0.24 separates every time I think, it just recovers better as more heavy layers are added. Which is precisely why I expect our "1 layer" variable choice to fail. That is my hypothesis at least, which we shall test.
coarse_recovery_hypothesis.scope: Derek's hypothesis; separation frequency and the required coarse-layer count are not measured
